description: A fast, asynchronous code formatting runner. Use Formatter Presets to enable popular formatters (prettierd, stylua, black, rustfmt, gofmt, biome, shfmt, sqlformat, clang-format) with zero Lua required, or use the Custom Formatters (Lua) escape hatch for full control. ⚠️ Prerequisites: You must install formatter binaries (prettierd, stylua, black, etc.) separately via your package manager. This plugin only executes CLI commands — it does not install them for you.
author: mhartington
tagline: Async code formatter runner — pick presets or write custom Lua for any filetype

generationRules.message: Raw Lua in 'Custom Formatters (Lua)' overrides 'Formatter Presets'. Clear one to silence this warning.

options.label: Enable Logging
options.description: Write formatter activity to a log file. Useful for debugging formatter issues. The log file path is shown in :messages after a format.

options.label: Log Level
options.description: Controls how verbose the log output is. Values: 0=TRACE (most verbose), 1=DEBUG, 2=INFO, 3=WARN (default — only problems), 4=ERROR, 5=OFF (no logging). Lower values log more.

options.label: Formatter Presets
options.description: Map filetypes to built-in formatter.nvim presets using structured rows. Multiple rows for the same filetype run in order. The wildcard '*' applies to all filetypes. ⚠️ Each preset shells out to a CLI binary you must install yourself.

conflictGroups.message: Filetype '{{key}}' has multiple competing formatter presets. Confirm this is intentional.

options.label: Custom Formatters (Lua)
options.description: Custom Lua override for the entire 'filetype' table. If non-empty, this REPLACES the rows above (a warning will be emitted). Use only when the curated rows can't express your need.

functions.name: format
functions.label: Format Buffer
functions.description: Format the current buffer using the configured formatters for its filetype
functions.whatItDoes: Runs all formatter functions mapped to the current buffer's filetype, applying the result asynchronously. Equivalent to :Format.

functions.name: format_write
functions.label: Format and Save
functions.description: Format the current buffer and write it to disk
functions.whatItDoes: Formats the current buffer and immediately saves it. Equivalent to :FormatWrite. Useful as an action in a BufWritePost autocmd graph node.

functions.name: format_lock
functions.label: Format Buffer (Locked)
functions.description: Format the current buffer with buffer locking enabled
functions.whatItDoes: Marks the buffer as non-modifiable while formatting runs, preventing concurrent edits. Equivalent to :FormatLock.

functions.name: format_write_lock
functions.label: Format, Lock and Save
functions.description: Format with buffer locking and write to disk
functions.whatItDoes: Combines buffer locking, formatting, and saving in one operation. Equivalent to :FormatWriteLock.

functionTemplates.label: Format on Save
functionTemplates.shortDescription: Format and save the buffer (use inside a BufWritePost autocmd node)
functionTemplates.whatItDoes: Triggers :FormatWrite — typically wired as the action of a BufWritePost autocmd so files are always formatted when saved.

exCommands.name: Format
exCommands.description: Format the current buffer using the configured formatters for its filetype. Runs asynchronously and does not save the file.

exCommands.name: FormatWrite
exCommands.description: Format the current buffer and write (save) it. The file is saved after all formatters complete. Commonly used in BufWritePost autocmds for format-on-save behavior.

exCommands.name: FormatLock
exCommands.description: Format the current buffer with buffer locking. Sets 'modifiable' to false while formatting runs, preventing edits from interfering with the formatter output.

exCommands.name: FormatWriteLock
exCommands.description: Format the current buffer with buffer locking, then write it to disk. Combines the safety of FormatLock with the convenience of FormatWrite.
